clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy woman in her 40s developed intense occipital headache and progressive lower limb weakness a day after receiving the AZD1222 SARS-CoV-2 vaccine. Initial brain MRI showed juxtacortical, deep subcortical white matter, corpus callosum, and cerebral peduncle lesions. No optic neuritis symptoms were reported. Two months later, after stopping oral prednisone, she worsened with quadriplegia, sensory level at C4, and bladder/bowel involvement. Serum AQP4-IgG antibody was positive by cell-based assay, with other autoantibodies negative. Follow-up MRI showed increased cerebral lesions and significant longitudinally extensive cervical and dorsal spinal cord lesions. Routine blood tests and lumbar puncture, including oligoclonal bands, were unremarkable. These findings fulfilled diagnostic criteria for AQP4+ NMO.
